questions.question: What is the respiratory system?
questions.answer: The respiratory system is the body system responsible for breathing and exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: The lungs are the main organs of the respiratory system.
Which gas do humans inhale during breathing?
Fill in the blank: The ______ separates the chest cavity from the abdomen and helps in breathing.
What is the function of the lungs?
questions.answer: They exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide between the air and the blood.

questions.question: Observe the image and identify the organ shown.
Which image represents the trachea?
Breathing in is called inhalation.
Fill in the blank: Tiny air sacs in the lungs are called ______.
Where does the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide take place?
What is the function of the diaphragm?
questions.answer: It helps the lungs expand and contract during breathing.

questions.question: Carbon dioxide is removed from the body during exhalation.
Observe the image and identify the highlighted structure.
Which image shows the respiratory system?
Explain the difference between inhalation and exhalation.
questions.answer: Inhalation brings oxygen-rich air into the lungs, while exhalation removes carbon dioxide-rich air from the body.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Air enters the body through the ______ or mouth.
The trachea is also called the windpipe.
Which organ carries air from the nose to the lungs?
Why is the respiratory system important?
questions.answer: It supplies oxygen to the body and removes carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Explain how oxygen reaches the body's cells after entering the lungs.
questions.answer: Oxygen moves from the alveoli into the blood, which carries it to all body cells.
